assignedReviews.card_evidence: named after the scientist Henri Becquerel
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s

copy.en:
What unit measures radioactivity?

It's measured in becquerels (Bq), named after the scientist Henri Becquerel!
copy.tl:
Anong yunit ang sumusukat ng radioactivity?

Sinusukat ito sa becquerels (Bq), na ipinangalan kay Henri Becquerel!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga yunit ang nagsukod sa radioactivity?

Gisukod kini sa becquerels (Bq), nga ginganlan kang Henri Becquerel!

copy.en: Once a Rafflesia blooms, its flower stays open for only a few days before it wilts.
copy.tl: Kapag namulaklak na ang Rafflesia, ang bulaklak nito ay bukas lang ng ilang araw bago ito malanta.
copy.bis: Kon mamuklad na ang Rafflesia, ang bulak niini magpabilin nga bukas sa pipila lang ka adlaw una malaya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: helping its foul smell spread faster to attract flies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Attracting flies is adjacent to pollination; pollen, seed production, and propagation are never named.

copy.en:
Why does the Rafflesia flower give off heat?

When its bud opens, the Rafflesia flower gives off a little heat, helping its foul smell spread faster to attract flies.
copy.tl:
Bakit gumagawa ng init ang bulaklak ng Rafflesia?

Kapag bumukadkad ang buko nito, nakakapagbigay ng kaunting init ang bulaklak ng Rafflesia, na tumutulong para mas mabilis kumalat ang mabahong amoy nito at maakit ang mga langaw.
copy.bis:
Nganong mohatag og init ang bulak sa Rafflesia?

Kung mamukhad ang buko niini, ang bulak sa Rafflesia makahatag og gamay nga kainit, nga motabang aron mas paspas mokatag ang baho niini ug makadani og mga langaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It has no leaves, stems, or roots
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that Rafflesia lacks leaves, stems, and roots, but it does not teach the roles of these outer plant parts in obtaining water and nutrients. It only touches on plant-part vocabulary without supporting the competency's observation and function skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's a parasite that grows inside its host vine
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: Parasitism is not presented as an adaptation to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods. The card does not explain how Rafflesia's parasitic lifestyle helps it survive environmental stress, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
What is the world's biggest single flower?

Rafflesia! It has no leaves, stems, or roots—it's a parasite that grows inside its host vine.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking solong bulaklak sa mundo?

Ang Rafflesia! Walang dahon, tangkay, o ugat ito—parasite itong lumalaki sa loob ng host na Tetrastigma vine.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga solong bulak sa kalibutan?

Ang Rafflesia! Walay dahon, tangkay, o gamot kini—parasite nga motubo sa sulod sa host nga Tetrastigma vine.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Rafflesia has no leaves, stems, or roots of its own
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves, stems, and roots only to state that Rafflesia lacks them. It does not describe the outer parts of plants or their roles in getting water and nutrients, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Rafflesia has no leaves, stems, or roots of its own

assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe the purpose of any specialized plant structure such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots. It only notes the absence of typical plant organs in Rafflesia, which is not instructional for this competency.

copy.en: The Rafflesia has no leaves, stems, or roots of its own — almost all we ever see of it is the giant flower.
copy.tl: Ang Rafflesia ay walang sariling dahon, tangkay, o ugat, kaya halos bulaklak lang ang nakikita natin.
copy.bis: Ang Rafflesia walay kaugalingong dahon, punoan, o gamot, busa halos bulak ra ang atong makita.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the open Rafflesia flower lasts only a few days before it wilts and rots
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Bloom duration is flowering timing, not pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its bud grows for a long time, the open Rafflesia flower lasts only a few days
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: Bud-to-wilt timing is one plant stage, not a comparison of mammal, bird, and plant life cycles.

copy.en:
How long does a Rafflesia bloom last?

Even though its bud grows for a long time, the open Rafflesia flower lasts only a few days before it wilts and rots -- so seeing one in bloom is super lucky!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal namumukadkad ang Rafflesia?

Kahit matagal lumaki ang usbong nito, ang bukad na Rafflesia ay ilang araw lang bago manlanta at mabulok -- kaya sobrang swerte kung makakita ka nito!
copy.bis:
Hangtod kanus-a molungtad ang bukad nga Rafflesia?

Bisan dugay motubo ang usbong niini, ang bukad nga bulak sa Rafflesia molungtad lang og pipila ka adlaw una malaya ug madunot -- mao nga swerte kaayo kon makakita ka niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sunflower is only about as big as a plate, but a Rafflesia flower can grow even bigger than a car tire
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: Flower size is not leaves, roots, or stems taking water and nutrients from soil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a Rafflesia flower can grow even bigger than a car tire — and instead of smelling sweet, it stinks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: Flower size and stink are not rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: instead of smelling sweet, it stinks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Size trivia and smell without pollen is not pollination, seed production, or plant propagation as methods.

copy.en:
How big can a Rafflesia flower grow?

A sunflower is only about as big as a plate, but a Rafflesia flower can grow even bigger than a car tire — and instead of smelling sweet, it stinks!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalaki ang bulaklak ng Rafflesia?

Kasinlaki lang ng plato ang sunflower, pero ang bulaklak ng Rafflesia ay mas malaki pa sa gulong ng kotse — at sa halip na mabango, mabaho pa ito!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadako ang bulak sa Rafflesia?

Sama lang kadako sa plato ang mirasol, apan ang bulak sa Rafflesia mas dako pa sa ligid sa awto — ug imbis nga humot, mobaho hinuon kini!

copy.en: Remember the order of rainbow colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet!
copy.tl: Tandaan ang pagkakasunod ng kulay ng bahaghari: pula, kahel, dilaw, berde, asul, indigo, at violet!
copy.bis: Hinumdomi ang han-ay sa kolor sa balangaw: pula, kahel, dalag, berde, asul, indigo, ug violet!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rainbow forms when sunlight refracts into a raindrop, reflects inside it, and refracts out again

copy.en: A rainbow forms when sunlight refracts into a raindrop, reflects inside it, and refracts out again — splitting white light into all its beautiful colours!
copy.tl: Ang bahaghari ay nabubuo kapag ang liwanag ng araw ay nagrerefract papasok sa patak ng ulan, sumasalamin sa loob, at nagrerefract uli papalabas — hinahati-hati ang puting liwanag sa lahat ng magagandang kulay!
copy.bis: Ang bahaghari nahimo kung ang kahayag sa adlaw nagarefrakt papasulod sa patak sa ulan, nagasalamin sa sulod, ug nagarefrakt paguwa pag-usab — gibuak ang puting suga sa tanan niyang nindot nga mga kolor!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rainbow forms when sunlight refracts and splits into beautiful colors inside raindrops!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions refraction as the cause of a rainbow, which is an everyday example of refraction, but the competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection using mirrors and refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms. The card provides no investigation, no equipment, and no illustration of the phenomena; it only states a fact about rainbows.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A rainbow forms when sunlight refracts and splits into beautiful colors inside raindrops!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how light behaves (refraction and splitting) in a rainbow, which touches on light behavior, but the competency requires participating in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses. copy.en:
How does a rainbow form?

A rainbow forms when sunlight refracts and splits into beautiful colors inside raindrops!
copy.tl:
Paano nabubuo ang bahaghari?

Nabubuo ang bahaghari kapag ang liwanag ng araw ay lumiliko at nahahati sa mga kulay sa loob ng mga patak ng ulan!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagporma ang balangaw?

Maporma ang balangaw kon ang kahayag sa adlaw mobawog ug mabahin sa mga kolor sa sulod sa mga tulo sa ulan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A beautiful rainbow always has exactly 7 colors!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the relative wavelengths and frequencies of different types of electromagnetic waves, including radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, x-rays, and gamma radiation

copy.en: A beautiful rainbow always has exactly 7 colors!
copy.tl: Ang magandang bahaghari ay palaging may 7 na kulay!
copy.bis: Ang nindot nga balangaw kanunay adunay 7 ka kolor!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Monkeys, birds, and bats often live high in the rainforest canopy

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Monkeys, birds, and bats often live high in the rainforest canopy

copy.en: Monkeys, birds, and bats often live high in the rainforest canopy and rarely ever come down to the ground.
copy.tl: Maraming unggoy, ibon, at paniki ay nakatira sa canopy ng gubat at bihira lang bumaba sa lupa.
copy.bis: Daghang amo, langgam, ug kabog nagpuyo sa canopy sa lasang ug talagsa ra molugsong sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: dead leaves and animals rot super fast in the heat and moisture, and roots quickly soak up the nutrients

assignedReviews.reason: Fast rotting and nutrient recycling without naming decomposers is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: dead leaves and animals rot super fast in the heat and moisture, and roots quickly soak up the nutrients

assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use flow charts or labeled diagrams of the carbon, oxygen, or water cycles.

copy.en: In a rainforest, dead leaves and animals rot super fast in the heat and moisture, and roots quickly soak up the nutrients — that's why the soil stays thin even though nutrients get recycled so rapidly!
copy.tl: Sa rainforest, napakabilis mabulok ng patay na dahon at hayop dahil sa init at halumigmig, at agad sinasalo ng mga ugat ang sustansya — kaya manipis lang ang lupa kahit mabilis itong nire-recycle!
copy.bis: Sa rainforest, paspas kaayong madunot ang patay nga dahon ug hayop tungod sa init ug umog, ug dali-dali gisuyop sa mga gamot ang sustansya — mao nga nipis ra ang yuta bisan paspas kining gi-recycle!

copy.en: Rambutan is a fruit with a skin covered in soft, hair-like spines.
copy.tl: Ang rambutan ay isang prutas na may balat na parang may malambot na buhok o tinik.
copy.bis: Ang rambutan usa ka prutas nga may panit nga daw adunay humok nga balahibo o tunok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An eagle's bones are light and partly hollow inside, making it easier for it to fly and soar in the sky.

copy.en:
Why can eagles fly so easily?

An eagle's bones are light and partly hollow inside, making it easier for it to fly and soar in the sky.
copy.tl:
Bakit madaling lumipad ang agila?

Magaan at parang guwang sa loob ang mga buto ng agila kaya mas madali itong lumipad at lumutang sa himpapawid.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga sayon lang molupad ang agila?

Gaan ug daw guwang sa sulod ang mga bukog sa agila busa mas sayon kining makalupad ug makalutaw sa kawanangan.

copy.en: Rattan loves warm, moist rainforests — you'll find many kinds growing wild across the Philippines and Southeast Asia!
copy.tl: Mahilig tumubo ang uway sa mainit at mahalumigmig na kagubatan — marami nito sa mga gubat ng Pilipinas at Timog-Silangang Asya!
copy.bis: Ganahan motubo ang uway sa init ug umog nga kalasangan — daghan niini sa mga lasang sa Pilipinas ug Habagatan-Sidlakang Asya!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rattan (uway or yantok) is a palm that climbs up other trees in the forest
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that rattan climbs, but it does not name or describe the purpose of any specialized plant structure (rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, aerial roots, etc.). It only gives a general observation about the plant's climbing habit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rattan (uway or yantok) is a palm that climbs up other trees in the forest
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not discuss outer plant parts such as leaves, roots, or stems, nor their role in obtaining water and nutrients. It only states that rattan is a climbing palm, which is not directly about the function of plant parts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rattan (uway or yantok) is a palm that climbs up other trees in the forest
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes rattan's climbing habit but does not explain how it is adapted to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods. Climbing is not presented as an adaptation to any specific environmental stress.

copy.en: Rattan (uway or yantok) is a palm that climbs up other trees in the forest — so it looks more like a vine than a regular standing tree.
copy.tl: Ang rattan (uway o yantok) ay isang uri ng palma na umaakyat sa ibang puno sa gubat, kaya parang baging ang hitsura nito kaysa karaniwang puno.
copy.bis: Ang rattan (uway o yantok) usa ka matang sa palma nga mosaka sa ubang kahoy sa lasang, mao nga morag baging hinuon kini kaysa ordinaryong kahoy.

copy.en: Before starting, read the full 'what we need to do' list aloud! This ensures even the quietest group members hear the plan.
copy.tl: Bago magsimula, basahin nang malakas ang buong listahan ng 'ano ang gagawin'! Para marinig din ng mga tahimik na kasamahan ang plano.
copy.bis: Una magsugod, basaha og kusog ang kompleto nga lista sa 'unsa ang buhaton'! Aron madungog usab sa mga hilum nga kauban ang plano.

assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about real vs virtual images in a flat mirror, which touches on reflection, but it does not support the competency's requirement to carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection using plane and curved mirrors and refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms. copy.en: A real image can be projected onto a screen, but a virtual image in a flat mirror cannot be caught on a screen!
copy.tl: Ang real image ay maaaring iproject sa screen, pero ang virtual image sa patag na salamin ay hindi mahuhuli sa screen!
copy.bis: Ang real image mapakita sa screen, apan ang virtual image sa patag nga salamin dili madakop sa screen!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: where the sepals, petals, stamens, and pistils all attach

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil

copy.en:
What is the receptacle of a flower?

The receptacle is the wide tip at the end of the flower stalk where the sepals, petals, stamens, and pistils all attach!
copy.tl:
Ano ang receptacle ng bulaklak?

Ang receptacle ay ang pinalapad na dulo ng tangkay ng bulaklak kung saan nakakabit ang mga sepal, petal, stamen, at pistil!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang receptacle sa bulak?

Ang receptacle mao ang pinalapad nga dulo sa tangkay sa bulak diin nakadugtong ang mga sepal, petal, stamen, ug pistil!

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions breakdown and microbial spoilage, which are chemical/biochemical processes, but it does not explain any factor affecting the rate of a chemical reaction (e.g., temperature, concentration, surface area) nor apply it to food preservation, materials production, fire, pollution, or corrosion. assignedReviews.reason: The card describes degradation of a material (anthocyanin) and spoilage by microbes, which touches on degradability, but it does not describe chemical properties such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable in the sense of the competency. It is about an indicator losing effectiveness, not a general material property.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Over time, anthocyanin breaks down and microbes spoil it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions breakdown and spoilage, which are chemical changes, but it does not explain reversibility or irreversibility of physical vs. chemical changes. copy.en:
Why does old cabbage juice stop working?

Over time, anthocyanin breaks down and microbes spoil it. That's why it's best to use fresh juice or keep it in the fridge!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi na gumagana ang lumang katas ng repolyo?

Sa paglipas ng panahon, nasisira ang anthocyanin at sinisira ito ng mga mikrobyo. Kaya mas mainam gumamit ng sariwa o itago sa ref!
copy.bis:
Nganong dili na molihok ang daan nga duga sa repolyo?

Sa paglabay sa panahon, maguba ang anthocyanin ug madumot sa mga mikrobyo. Mao nga mas maayo mogamit og bag-o o itago sa ref!

copy.tl: Malaki ang epekto ng red tide sa mga mangingisda at nagtitinda ng tahong — kapag may babala, hindi sila makakapagbenta ng kabibe at nawawalan sila ng kita habang tumatagal ito.
copy.bis: Dako ang epekto sa red tide sa mga mananagat ug tigbaligya og tahong — kon naay pasidaan, dili sila makabaligya og kabibe ug mawad-an sila og kita samtang nagpadayon kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's caused by too much plankton

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Red tide isn't about tides or waves at all—it's caused by too much plankton
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight

It does not involve locating or describing non-living things such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, or sunlight, nor any guided activity. The tag is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Does red tide really come from tides?

No! Red tide isn't about tides or waves at all—it's caused by too much plankton, so a better name for it is harmful algal bloom.
copy.tl:
Talaga bang galing sa taog ang red tide?

Hindi! Hindi tungkol sa taog o alon ang red tide—ang dahilan ay ang sobrang dami ng plankton, kaya mas tamang tawag dito ay harmful algal bloom.
copy.bis:
Tinuod ba nga gikan sa sulog ang red tide?

Dili! Dili bahin sa sulog o balod ang red tide—ang hinungdan mao ang sobra nga plankton, mao nga mas sakto nga tawag niini mao ang harmful algal bloom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: doctors can only help patients breathe

assignedReviews.reason: Card mentions helping patients breathe but does not identify respiratory system parts (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: avoiding it matters so much

assignedReviews.reason: Card emphasizes avoiding red tide poisoning, not protecting or conserving the environment for living things to survive.

copy.en: There's no medicine or antidote that can cure red tide poisoning — doctors can only help patients breathe and stay alive while the body slowly clears the toxin, which is why avoiding it matters so much.
copy.tl: Walang direktang gamot o antidote na pumapatay sa lason ng red tide — sa ospital, tinutulungan lang ang pasyente na makahinga habang dahan-dahang inaalis ng katawan ang lason, kaya napakahalaga ng pag-iwas.
copy.bis: Walay direkta nga tambal o antidote nga makapatay sa hilo sa red tide — sa ospital, tabangan lang ang pasyente nga makaginhawa samtang hinay-hinay nga gihawa sa lawas ang hilo, mao nga importante kaayo ang pag-likay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: anyone who eats toxic shellfish can be poisoned
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions harm from eating toxic shellfish, but its focus is distinguishing red tide poisoning from seafood allergy, not explaining how interactions between living things bring harm. It does not teach the interaction concept or its good/harm effects.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes poisoning symptoms, not how any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) works. It does not support the competency.

copy.en: Red tide poisoning isn't the same as a seafood allergy. With an allergy, only some people react, usually with rashes or itching. With red tide, anyone who eats toxic shellfish can be poisoned, with symptoms of numbness and muscle weakness — not itching.
copy.tl: Iba ang pagkalason sa red tide sa allergy sa seafood. Sa allergy, iilan lang ang apektado, karaniwang pamamantal o pangangati. Sa red tide, kahit sino ang kumain ng may-lasong kabibe ay puwedeng malason, at ang sintomas ay pamamanhid at panghihina ng kalamnan — hindi pangangati.
copy.bis: Lahi ang pagkahilo sa red tide sa allergy sa seafood. Sa allergy, pipila ra ang maapektuhan, kasagaran pamuti o katol. Sa red tide, bisan kinsa nga mokaon og may-hilo nga kinhason mahimong mahilo, ug ang simtomas mao ang pagkamanhod ug kaluya sa kaunoran — dili katol.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Reef fish have very good color vision, and they use their bright colors to recognize their own kind, find a mate, or warn others
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the current function of bright colors in reef fish (recognition, mating, warning) but does not describe how animals have changed over time to better suit their environment, nor does it mention mimicry or camouflage. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Reef fish have very good color vision, and they use their bright colors to recognize their own kind, find a mate, or warn others
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce

copy.en:
Why are reef fish so colorful?

Reef fish have very good color vision, and they use their bright colors to recognize their own kind, find a mate, or warn others — the colors aren't just decoration.
copy.tl:
Bakit makukulay ang mga isda sa bahura?

Maganda ang paningin ng mga isda sa bahura sa kulay, at ginagamit nila ang matingkad na kulay para makilala ang kapwa nila isda, makahanap ng kapareha, o magbabala — hindi lang ito pampaganda.
copy.bis:
Nganong kolorido ang mga isda sa bahura?

Maayo kaayo ang panan-aw sa mga isda sa bahura sa kolor, ug gigamit nila ang hayag nga kolor aron mailhan ang ilang kauban, makakita og kapareha, o magpasidaan — dili lang kini pandekorasyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This protects it from germs and disease and helps it swim faster
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a current protective feature (mucus coat) of fish, but does not discuss how animals have changed over time to suit their environment. It lacks any evolutionary or adaptive-change context, so it does not directly support the competency's focus on examples of animals having changed to better suit their environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A thin layer of mucus coats a fish's skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a fish's skin but does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in movement or gathering food. The mucus coat's role in protection and swimming speed is not the same as identifying body parts and their roles for movement and food gathering.

copy.en: A thin layer of mucus coats a fish's skin, making it feel slippery. This protects it from germs and disease and helps it swim faster — which is why we shouldn't touch fish, since it rubs off this protection.
copy.tl: May manipis na uhog na bumabalot sa balat ng isda, kaya ito madulas. Pinoprotektahan nito ang isda laban sa mikrobyo at sakit at tinutulungan itong lumangoy nang mas mabilis — kaya nga huwag hawakan ang isda, dahil natatanggal ang proteksyong ito.
copy.bis: Adunay nipis nga uhog nga naglukop sa panit sa isda, mao nga danlog kini. Nanalipod kini sa isda batok sa mikrobyo ug sakit ug motabang niini molangoy og mas paspas — mao nga dili nato hikapon ang isda, kay matangtang ang panalipod niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Unlike ordinary fish with hard bones, a reef shark's skeleton is made of cartilage
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)

assignedReviews.reason: Cartilage versus hard bone in two fish is not animals with a backbone versus animals without backbones.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: making it lighter and easier to move

assignedReviews.reason: Lighter cartilage is not mimicry or camouflage.

copy.en:
What is a shark's skeleton made of?

Unlike ordinary fish with hard bones, a reef shark's skeleton is made of cartilage — the same bendy material in our nose and ears — making it lighter and easier to move!
copy.tl:
Ano ang gawa sa kalansay ng pating?

Hindi tulad ng ordinaryong isda na may matigas na buto, ang kalansay ng reef shark ay gawa sa cartilage — ang parehong malambot na materyal sa ilong at tainga natin — kaya mas magaan at madali itong kumilos!
copy.bis:
Unsay hinimoan sa kalabera sa iho?

Dili sama sa ordinaryong isda nga adunay gahi nga bukog, ang kalabera sa reef shark hinimo sa cartilage — ang samang humok nga materyal sa atong ilong ug dalunggan — mao nga mas gaan ug mas sayon molihok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The spinal cord is responsible for a reflex action, an instantaneous movement that protects the body from harm.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific nervous system mechanism (reflex action) rather than teaching the general characteristic of living things responding. copy.en: The spinal cord is responsible for a reflex action, an instantaneous movement that protects the body from harm.
copy.tl: Ang spinal cord ang responsable para sa reflex action, isang agarang paggalaw na nagpoprotekta sa katawan mula sa panganib.
copy.bis: Ang spinal cord maoy responsable sa reflex action, usa ka diha-diha nga paglihok nga nagprotektar sa lawas batok sa kadaot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Reflexes are natural; you're born already having them.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses reflexes as inborn responses, but does not describe the general characteristic that living things respond, nor does it address growth or reproduction. It only touches on a specific type of response without connecting it to the competency's broader concept.

copy.en:
Do you need to practice a reflex to have one?

No — many think we learn reflexes like we learn to read, but that's not true. Reflexes are natural; you're born already having them.
copy.tl:
Kailangan bang sanayin ang reflex?

Hindi — inaakala ng marami na natututo tayo ng reflex tulad ng pagbabasa, pero hindi totoo iyon. Likas ang reflex; taglay mo na ito noong ipinanganak ka.
copy.bis:
Kinahanglan ba nga bansayon ang reflex?

Dili — daghan ang naghunahuna nga makat-on ta og reflex sama sa pagbasa, apan dili kana tinuod. Natural ang reflex; dala nimo na kini sukad pagkatawo.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes parts of a reflex arc working together, but G8-L-2 requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together, with examples such as digestion and excretion. assignedReviews.card_evidence: the receptor that senses
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sensing, which relates to responding, but G3-L-3 requires describing the characteristics of living things: grow, respond, and reproduce. The card does not teach these characteristics as a general concept; it only describes a specific reflex mechanism, which is not direct support for the Grade 3 competency.

copy.en: A reflex has five parts working together like a relay: the receptor that senses, the sensory neuron carrying the signal in, the spinal cord that processes it, the motor neuron carrying the order out, and the muscle that acts.
copy.tl: May limang bahagi ang reflex na magkadugtong parang relay: ang receptor na nakaramdam, ang sensory neuron na nagdadala ng signal papasok, ang gulugod na nagpoproseso, ang motor neuron na nagdadala ng utos palabas, at ang kalamnan na kumikilos.
copy.bis: Adunay lima ka bahin ang reflex nga nagdugtong sama sa relay: ang receptor nga makabati, ang sensory neuron nga modala sa signal pasulod, ang gulugod nga moproseso, ang motor neuron nga modala sa mando pagawas, ug ang kaunoran nga molihok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a sensory neuron carries the signal to your spinal cord, and a motor neuron passes the command on to your muscle
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a reflex arc involving sensory and motor neurons, spinal cord, and muscle. It does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and it does not explain how body systems work together such as digestion and excretion. The content is only broadly related to body systems.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a sensory neuron carries the signal to your spinal cord, and a motor neuron passes the command on to your muscle
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions neurons and spinal cord, which are parts of biological organization, but it does not use a labelled diagram to describe connections between levels of biological organization from cells to the biosphere. It does not directly support the competency's required representation or scope.

copy.en: In a reflex, a sensory neuron carries the signal to your spinal cord, and a motor neuron passes the command on to your muscle.
copy.tl: Sa reflex, dinadala ng sensory neuron ang senyas papunta sa gulugod, at ipinapasa ng motor neuron ang utos sa kalamnan.
copy.bis: Sa reflex, gidala sa sensory neuron ang senyas paingon sa dugokan sa likod, ug gipasa sa motor neuron ang mando ngadto sa kaunuran.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You don't choose to shiver — your body does it on its own

assignedReviews.reason: The card states that shivering is involuntary, which is tangentially related to body temperature regulation, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor does it mention indicators like body temperature, glucose, or blood pressure. assignedReviews.card_evidence: You don't choose to shiver — your body does it on its own
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how homeostasis is maintained through various feedback mechanisms, both positive and negative
assignedReviews.reason: Shivering is a homeostatic response, but the card does not explain feedback mechanisms (positive or negative) or how homeostasis is maintained. It only notes that shivering is automatic, which is background knowledge at most, not direct support for explaining feedback mechanisms.

copy.en:
Bakit hindi mapigilan ang panginginig?

You don't choose to shiver — your body does it on its own, which is why it's so hard to stop shivering when you're truly cold.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi mapigilan ang panginginig?

Hindi mo pinipili ang manginig — kusa itong ginagawa ng katawan mo, kaya mahirap itong pigilan kapag talagang nilalamig ka.
copy.bis:
Nganong dili mapugngan ang pagkurog?

Dili nimo pilion ang mokurog — kusog kining gibuhat sa imong lawas, mao nga lisod pugngan kon tinuod nga gitugnaw ka.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The gag reflex pushes food back out when it goes down the wrong way, so you don't choke.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the gag reflex preventing choking, but does not identify or describe any parts of the digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) or how they work. It is only tangentially related to the digestive tract.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The gag reflex pushes food back out when it goes down the wrong way, so you don't choke.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions protecting the airway from choking, but does not identify or describe any parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work. It is only tangentially related to respiratory protection.

copy.en: The gag reflex pushes food back out when it goes down the wrong way, so you don't choke.
copy.tl: Ang gag reflex ay nagtataboy ng pagkain palabas kapag napunta ito sa maling daanan, para hindi ka mabulunan.
copy.bis: Ang gag reflex magtuklod sa pagkaon pabalik kung moadto kini sa sayop nga agianan, aron dili ka mabara.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Refraction is the bending of light when it passes from one material into another
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications

copy.en:
What is refraction?

Refraction is the bending of light when it passes from one material into another, like traveling from air into water!
copy.tl:
Ano ang refraction?

Ang refraction ay ang pagbaluktot ng liwanag kapag lumipas ito mula sa isang materyal papunta sa isa pa, tulad ng hangin papuntang tubig!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang refraction?

Ang refraction mao ang pagbalog sa suga kung moagi kini gikan sa usa ka materyal ngadto sa lain, sama sa hangin ngadto sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can spot it in a bent-looking straw in a glass, eyeglasses, cameras, and even a rainbow in the sky!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card only lists everyday examples of refraction. It does not support the competency's core action of carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms, nor does it describe or illustrate the phenomenon itself.

copy.en:
Where can we see refraction every day?

You can spot it in a bent-looking straw in a glass, eyeglasses, cameras, and even a rainbow in the sky!
copy.tl:
Saan natin makikita ang refraction araw-araw?

Makikita mo ito sa straw na mukhang baluktot sa baso, salamin sa mata, kamera, at bahaghari sa langit!
copy.bis:
Asa nato makita ang refraction kada adlaw?

Makita nimo kini sa straw nga morag baluktot sa baso, antiyohos, kamera, ug balangaw sa langit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When light travels from air into water, it changes direction and bends just a little bit. We call this cool trick refraction!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a basic fact about refraction (light bending when entering water), but the competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with everyday examples. The card does not involve any investigation, illustration, or the specified apparatus, so it only shares the general topic of refraction without directly supporting the competency's required activity.

copy.en: When light travels from air into water, it changes direction and bends just a little bit. We call this cool trick refraction!
copy.tl: Kapag ang liwanag ay dumadaan mula sa hangin papuntang tubig, nagbabago ito ng direksyon at bahagyang nagbabaluktot. Tinatawag natin itong refraction!
copy.bis: Kon ang kahayag moagi gikan sa hangin paingon sa tubig, mausab kini sa direksyon ug gamay nga mobawog. Gitawag nato kini nga refraction!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because of refraction, the fish looks higher and closer than its real spot underwater.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions refraction and gives an everyday application (spearing fish), but the competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection/refraction using specific equipment (mirrors, blocks, lenses, prisms). The card provides no investigation, equipment, or illustration, so it only shares the topic of refraction without directly supporting the required skill.

copy.en: Traditional Filipino fishers know to aim a little lower when spearing fish! Because of refraction, the fish looks higher and closer than its real spot underwater.
copy.tl: Alam ng mga tradisyonal na mangingisdang Pilipino na tumira nang bahagyang mas mababa kapag nanganga! Dahil sa refraction, mukhang mas mataas at malapit ang isda kaysa sa totoong pwesto nito.
copy.bis: Nahibalo ang tradisyonal nga mangingisdang Pilipino nga motira og gamay nga ubos kung mamana! Tungod sa refraction, morag mas taas ug duol ang isda kaysa sa tinuod nga pwesto niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In reflection, light bounces back off a surface like a mirror. But in refraction, light passes through into another material and bends instead of bouncing back!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the basic conceptual difference between reflection and refraction, which is useful background knowledge. However, the competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection using plane/curved mirrors and refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with everyday examples. The card does not involve any investigation, illustration, or use of the specified equipment, so it only provides prerequisite conceptual support.

copy.en:
How are refraction and reflection different?

In reflection, light bounces back off a surface like a mirror. But in refraction, light passes through into another material and bends instead of bouncing back!
copy.tl:
Paano magkaiba ang refraction at reflection?

Sa reflection, tumatalbog pabalik ang liwanag sa surface parang salamin. Sa refraction naman, tumatawid ang liwanag sa ibang materyales at yumuyuko doon sa halip na bumalik!
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa refraction ug reflection?

Sa reflection, mubalik og bundak ang kahayag sa surface sama sa salamin. Sa refraction, mutadlas ang kahayag sa laing materyales ug mubawog doon sa dili mubalik!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That's a mirage caused by refraction!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a mirage as an everyday example of refraction, but the competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection/refraction using specific equipment (mirrors, transparent blocks, lenses, prisms). The card provides no investigation, equipment, or illustration of the phenomena beyond a conceptual explanation, so it does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en:
Why does a hot road look like it has a puddle of water?

That's a mirage caused by refraction! Hot air near the ground bends light from the sky upward into your eye, making it look like water.
copy.tl:
Bakit parang may tubig sa mainit na kalsada?

Malikmata 'yan dahil sa refraction! Ang mainit na hangin malapit sa lupa ay binabaluktot ang liwanag mula sa langit pataas sa mata mo, kaya parang may tubig.
copy.bis:
Nganong morag may tubig sa mainit nga karsada?

Malikmata na tungod sa refraction! Ang init nga hangin duol sa yuta gibawog ang kahayag gikan sa langit pataas sa imong mata, mao nga morag may tubig.
